memory_update.text: LOPE is the cleanest direct public-company mapping for outsourced online higher-education operating stack; later layers should test partner concentration, contract durability, enrollment quality, and regulatory risk.

COUR is a smaller-cap platform candidate for university degree, campus, and enterprise learning distribution, but its chokepoint status depends on proving durable university economics rather than broad learner traffic.

NNI is a low-attention hidden-infrastructure candidate because education technology, payments, student loan servicing, and systems workflows can be essential to the student lifecycle but are not usually screened as online education exposure.
ATGE should be treated primarily as a demand anchor/customer/operator for online and hybrid healthcare education infrastructure, not as a supplier pure-play.

Need a follow-up pass for delisted/private and recently distressed OPM peers, LMS/SIS vendors, enrollment marketing agencies, payment processors, proctoring/testing vendors, and clinical placement software providers; this pass stayed limited to direct US-listed public candidates.

node: Online higher-education fixed-cost stack: enrollment marketing, student services, course development, and student-information systems
summary: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the online higher-education fixed-cost stack. The strongest fit is Grand Canyon Education as a scaled university-services and online-program support provider. Coursera is a platform layer with university degree and enterprise/campus channels, but its exposure is broader than full OPM. Nelnet is a hidden infrastructure candidate through education technology, payments, loan servicing, systems, and data workflows. Adtalem is included as a direct online/postsecondary healthcare education operator and demand/customer anchor rather than a third-party supplier. No buy/sell view is implied.
